purpose: Feature: Fix this bug: Make the tutorial advance through claim, first cash-in, Dropper 2 buy, open SHOP, and buy a tier upgrade. Show the arrow and a visible Beam from the player to each target (the census must show beams > 0). Re-show a stuck step's hint after 15s. Fire shop_opened when the SHOP panel opens. Tutorial steps must reach 5+ in a 60s playtest, and the stale step-4 text must match the real action. -- Server-authoritative tutorial step driver. Steps: 1 claim a plot, 2 first cash-in, 3 buy Dropper 2, 4 open SHOP, 5 buy any tier upgrade other than Dropper 2, 6 done. API: TutorialFlow.start() (idempotent, guarded so it runs once), TutorialFlow.notify(player, eventName, arg) with eventName 'claimed' | 'cashed_in' | 'upgrade_bought' (arg is the upgrade id) | 'shop_opened', and TutorialFlow.getStep(player). start() creates the RemoteEvent ReplicatedStorage/ShopOpened. Its OnServerEvent handler is a server-validated 'shop_opened' notify that ignores repeats and anything outside step 4. Notify only advances when the event matches the current step, so repeats and out-of-order events are harmless. Per player it keeps the step index and step start time and mirrors them in the player attributes TutorialStep (number), TutorialText (string from TutorialConfig) and TutorialNonce (number). It keeps an ObjectValue 'TutorialTarget' under the player whose Value is the current target part, so the client can aim the beam. Targets: step 1 the nearest unclaimed claim gate part (found by searching Workspace for the claim gates PlazaBuilder made); step 2 the player's collector on the owned plot; step 3 the Dropper 2 pad on the owned plot; step 4 the owned plot's collector, so the beam stays visible while the client arrow points at the SHOP button; step 5 the first visible buy pad on the owned plot. Every 1s a loop checks each player. If a step has been unchanged for TutorialConfig.STUCK_RESHOW_SECONDS (15s) it re-shows the hint by re-setting TutorialText, incrementing TutorialNonce and bumping 'tutorial_reshown', then repeats every 15s. Fallbacks so the guide cannot stall: step 1 also advances if the player already owns a plot (the loop checks the plot owner), step 2 advances if the player's Cash has risen, and step 4 auto-advances after SHOP_STEP_FALLBACK_SECONDS (20s) if the SHOP was never opened. Each advance bumps 'tutorial_steps' via ForgeTelemetry. Reaching step 6 bumps 'tutorial_done'. A real shop open bumps 'shop_opened'. Cleans up on PlayerRemoving. Uses Players, ReplicatedStorage/TutorialConfig, ForgeTelemetry and Upgrades. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: tutorial_steps, shop_opened, tutorial_reshown, tutorial_done.
depends: ReplicatedStorage/TutorialConfig.luau, ReplicatedStorage/ForgeTelemetry.luau, ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades.luau

### ReplicatedStorage/ForgeTelemetry.luau
```luau
--!strict
-- ForgeTelemetry: tiny counter API for generated games. ForgeProbe reports these counters.
--
--   local ForgeTelemetry = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").ForgeTelemetry)
--   ForgeTelemetry.count("coins_collected")      -- +1
--   ForgeTelemetry.count("damage_dealt", 25)     -- +25
--   ForgeTelemetry.get()                          -- { coins_collected = 1, damage_dealt = 25 }
--
-- Counters live as number attributes on ServerStorage.ForgeCounters (a Folder), so every VM in the
-- server (game scripts, ForgeProbe, execute_luau) sees the same values. Server only: on the client
-- count() is a no-op and get() returns {}.

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local FOLDER_NAME = "ForgeCounters"

local ForgeTelemetry = {}

local function folder(): Instance?
	if not RunService:IsServer() then
		return nil
	end
	local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")
	local f = ServerStorage:FindFirstChild(FOLDER_NAME)
	if not f then
		f = Instance.new("Folder")
		f.Name = FOLDER_NAME
		f.Parent = ServerStorage
	end
	return f
end

-- Attribute names: letters, digits and underscores, max 100 chars, may not start with "RBX".
local function key(name: string): string
	local k = string.gsub(tostring(name), "[^%w_]", "_")
	if k == "" then
		k = "_"
	end
	if string.sub(k, 1, 3) == "RBX" then
		k = "_" .. k
	end
	return string.sub(k, 1, 100)
end

function ForgeTelemetry.count(name: string, n: number?)
	local f = folder()
	if not f then
		return
	end
	local ok = pcall(function()
		local k = key(name)
		local cur = f:GetAttribute(k)
		local add = tonumber(n) or 1
		f:SetAttribute(k, (if type(cur) == "number" then cur else 0) + add)
	end)
	if not ok then
		-- telemetry must never break the game
		return
	end
end

function ForgeTelemetry.get(): { [string]: number }
	local out: { [string]: number } = {}
	if not RunService:IsServer() then
		return out
	end
	local f = game:GetService("ServerStorage"):FindFirstChild(FOLDER_NAME)
	if not f then
		return out
	end
	for k, v in f:GetAttributes() do
		if type(v) == "number" then
			out[k] = v
		end
	end
	return out
end

return ForgeTelemetry
```

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull. Also keep the second purchase within about 20-30s of idle income, by raising per-item value or lowering the price, so the shop and later upgrades get exercised.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.
- Keep the time to first core-loop activity well inside the playtest window (the probe may last only ~6-15s). Any auto-claim or auto-start fallback should fire within a few seconds (about 3-5s, not 20s), and claim gates should sit near the spawn area, not far outside the plaza. An idle player must still reach the loop quickly. Keep the spec's auto-claim delay and the tested window consistent so the plaza state can still be observed before the claim.
- Budget the whole first-payout path, not just the claim: claim delay + first spawn + conveyor travel (length / speed) should land the first cash-in within about 3-4s of the claim. Use a short, fast conveyor, spawn the first item immediately on claim, and don't leave this borderline.
- Keep tutorial text consistent with the actual flow (e.g. don't say "walk to a gate" if auto-claim happens within seconds). Tutorial steps must be advanced by events that actually occur, or the player is left without guidance. Add a time-based fallback so a step can't stall. Make the steps lead the player to every key feature (buy pad, shop), and check that the guide beam or arrow actually appears (its census count is above 0).
- Feedback should be audible and visible: use verified sound ids from the shared asset table, not weak built-in rbxasset wavs. Add particles or ambient sparkle, and set the bloom threshold low enough that Neon parts glow.
- Shared effect helpers (burst, shake, sound, FOV punch) only matter if gameplay code calls them. Wire each helper to a real event (collect, buy, rebirth, big upgrade) and check that its counter is above 0 after a playtest. Big moments deserve stronger feedback than routine ones: camera shake, a shockwave ring, or a larger popup.

## Luau and Roblox APIs
- The base place is empty: build the map from code (Instance.new Parts, Anchored = true, parented to Workspace).
- Get services with game:GetService("Players") etc.; use task.wait / task.spawn / task.delay, never wait / spawn / delay.
- Players.PlayerAdded can fire before your script connects in a playtest: also loop over Players:GetPlayers() once at startup.
- Wait for characters with player.CharacterAdded (and player.Character if already present); use WaitForChild with a timeout across the client/server boundary.
- ModuleScripts must return exactly one value (usually a table); require them by path, e.g. require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Config")).
- Create RemoteEvents on the server in one place; clients only WaitForChild them and handle nil after the timeout.
- Bump counters for key gameplay events with require(ReplicatedStorage.ForgeTelemetry).count("name", 1) (server only) so playtests can verify the core loop. Include counters for purchases and other branches that need verification.
- Bump an effect counter (sound, burst, popup) where the effect is really created, not where the remote is fired. If the counter is high but the census shows 0 sounds or bursts, the effects are not real or are destroyed before they are counted. Fix the effect, don't trust the counter.
- Count each telemetry counter in exactly one place (the module that owns the event). Duplicate count calls push once-only counters past their expected value; a counter at 2x its expected value (e.g. 12 vs 6, or 2 claims for 1 player) means a double init, double build or duplicate timer, so check for it.
- Do not put telemetry or build side effects at the top level of a ModuleScript that is shared (e.g. a data module in ReplicatedStorage). Module top-level code can run once per environment or require path. Count inside the single builder function that the entry script calls once.
- Each builder/init function must be called exactly once from the entry script. If two modules both build the same thing (e.g. plaza and plot builders both building themes), assign ownership to one.
- Never call warn() or error() for expected situations such as a duplicate-startup guard. Warnings in the output fail "no errors or warnings" checks. Return silently or use print.

```luau
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local TutorialConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("TutorialConfig", 10))
local ForgeTelemetry = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ForgeTelemetry", 10))

local TutorialFlow = {}

local STUCK_SECONDS = (TutorialConfig :: any).STUCK_RESHOW_SECONDS or 15
local SHOP_FALLBACK = (TutorialConfig :: any).SHOP_STEP_FALLBACK_SECONDS or 20
local MAX_STEP = 6

local started = false
local states: { [Player]: any } = {}
local gateCache: { BasePart } = {}
local gateCacheTime = 0
local firstUpgradeId: string? = nil
local firstIdResolved = false

local EXTRA_TEXT = {
	[4] = "Tap the yellow SHOP button to open the shop!",
	[5] = "Buy a tier upgrade from the SHOP or a glowing pad!",
	[6] = "You're a tycoon now! Keep growing your factory!",
}

local function textFor(step: number): string
	if EXTRA_TEXT[step] then
		return EXTRA_TEXT[step]
	end
	local steps = (TutorialConfig :: any).STEPS
	local t = steps and steps[step]
	return if type(t) == "string" then t else ""
end

local function norm(s: any): string
	return string.lower((string.gsub(tostring(s), "[^%w]", "")))
end

local function resolveFirstId()
	if firstIdResolved then
		return
	end
	firstIdResolved = true
	pcall(function()
		local mod = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("Upgrades")
		if not mod then
			return
		end
		local U: any = require(mod)
		local arrays = { U.list, U.List, U.all, U.All, U }
		for _, arr in arrays do
			if type(arr) == "table" and type(arr[1]) == "table" then
				local e = arr[1]
				local id = e.id or e.Id or e.ID or e.name
				if id ~= nil then
					firstUpgradeId = tostring(id)
					return
				end
			end
		end
	end)
end

local function isDropper2(id: any): boolean
	resolveFirstId()
	if id == nil then
		return false
	end
	if firstUpgradeId and tostring(id) == firstUpgradeId then
		return true
	end
	local n = norm(id)
	return n == "dropper2" or n == "dropper02"
end

local function toPart(inst: Instance): BasePart?
	if inst:IsA("BasePart") then
		return inst
	elseif inst:IsA("Model") then
		return inst.PrimaryPart or inst:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("BasePart", true)
	end
	return nil
end

local OWNER_KEYS = { "OwnerUserId", "OwnerId", "Owner", "OwnerName", "ClaimedBy" }

local function ownedBy(inst: Instance, player: Player): boolean
	for _, k in OWNER_KEYS do
		local v = inst:GetAttribute(k)
		if v ~= nil and (v == player.UserId or v == player.Name) then
			return true
		end
	end
	local ov = inst:FindFirstChild("Owner")
	if ov then
		if ov:IsA("ObjectValue") and ov.Value == player then
			return true
		elseif ov:IsA("StringValue") and ov.Value == player.Name then
			return true
		elseif (ov:IsA("IntValue") or ov:IsA("NumberValue")) and (ov :: any).Value == player.UserId then
			return true
		end
	end
	local pn = player:GetAttribute("PlotName")
	if pn ~= nil and pn == inst.Name then
		return true
	end
	return false
end

local function hasAnyOwner(inst: Instance): boolean
	local cur: Instance? = inst
	for _ = 1, 3 do
		if not cur or cur == workspace then
			break
		end
		for _, k in OWNER_KEYS do
			local v = cur:GetAttribute(k)
			if v ~= nil and v ~= "" and v ~= 0 and v ~= false then
				return true
			end
		end
		cur = cur.Parent
	end
	return false
end

local function findOwnedPlot(player: Player): Instance?
	for _, c in workspace:GetChildren() do
		if c:IsA("Model") or c:IsA("Folder") then
			if ownedBy(c, player) and not c:IsA("Terrain") then
				if c:IsA("Model") or c.Name:lower():find("plot") then
					return c
				end
			end
			if c:IsA("Folder") then
				for _, cc in c:GetChildren() do
					if (cc:IsA("Model") or cc:IsA("Folder")) and ownedBy(cc, player) then
						return cc
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return nil
end

local function findInPlot(plot: Instance, pred: (Instance) -> boolean): BasePart?
	for _, d in plot:GetDescendants() do
		if (d:IsA("BasePart") or d:IsA("Model")) and pred(d) then
			local p = toPart(d)
			if p then
				return p
			end
		end
	end
	return nil
end

local function isCollector(d: Instance): boolean
	return string.find(string.lower(d.Name), "collector", 1, true) ~= nil
end

local function isPad(d: Instance): boolean
	if not d:IsA("BasePart") then
		return false
	end
	local lname = string.lower(d.Name)
	if string.find(lname, "collector", 1, true) then
		return false
	end
	return d:GetAttribute("UpgradeId") ~= nil or string.find(lname, "pad", 1, true) ~= nil
end

local function padIsDropper2(d: Instance): boolean
	local id = d:GetAttribute("UpgradeId")
	if id ~= nil and isDropper2(id) then
		return true
	end
	return norm(d.Name):find("dropper2", 1, true) ~= nil
end

local function visible(p: BasePart): boolean
	return p.Transparency < 0.95
end

local function nearestGate(player: Player): BasePart?
	if os.clock() - gateCacheTime > 3 or #gateCache == 0 then
		gateCache = {}
		gateCacheTime = os.clock()
		for _, d in workspace:GetDescendants() do
			if d:IsA("BasePart") then
				local ln = string.lower(d.Name)
				if d:GetAttribute("ClaimGate") ~= nil or string.find(ln, "gate", 1, true) then
					table.insert(gateCache, d)
				end
			end
		end
	end
	local char = player.Character
	local root = char and char:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	local origin = if root and root:IsA("BasePart") then root.Position else Vector3.zero
	local best, bestD, anyBest, anyD = nil, math.huge, nil, math.huge
	for _, g in gateCache do
		if g.Parent then
			local dist = (g.Position - origin).Magnitude
			if dist < anyD then
				anyBest, anyD = g, dist
			end
			if visible(g) and not hasAnyOwner(g) and dist < bestD then
				best, bestD = g, dist
			end
		end
	end
	return best or anyBest
end

local function computeTarget(player: Player, step: number): BasePart?
	if step == 1 then
		return nearestGate(player)
	end
	local plot = findOwnedPlot(player)
	if not plot then
		return nil
	end
	if step == 2 or step == 4 then
		return findInPlot(plot, isCollector)
	elseif step == 3 then
		local pad = findInPlot(plot, function(d)
			return isPad(d) and padIsDropper2(d)
		end)
		return pad or findInPlot(plot, isCollector)
	elseif step == 5 then
		local pad = findInPlot(plot, function(d)
			return isPad(d) and not padIsDropper2(d) and visible(d :: BasePart)
		end)
		return pad or findInPlot(plot, isCollector)
	end
	return nil
end

local function clearBeam(state)
	if state.beam then
		state.beam:Destroy()
		state.beam = nil
	end
	if state.att0 then
		state.att0:Destroy()
		state.att0 = nil
	end
	if state.att1 then
		state.att1:Destroy()
		state.att1 = nil
	end
	state.beamTarget = nil
end

local function updateBeam(player: Player, state, target: BasePart?)
	local char = player.Character
	local root = char and char:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	if not target or not target:IsDescendantOf(workspace) or not root or not root:IsA("BasePart") then
		clearBeam(state)
		return
	end
	if state.beam and state.beam.Parent and state.beamTarget == target and state.att0 and state.att0.Parent == root then
		return
	end
	clearBeam(state)
	local a0 = Instance.new("Attachment")
	a0.Name = "TutorialBeamStart"
	a0.Parent = root
	local a1 = Instance.new("Attachment")
	a1.Name = "TutorialBeamEnd_" .. player.UserId
	a1.Parent = target
	local beam = Instance.new("Beam")
	beam.Name = "TutorialBeam"
	beam.Attachment0 = a0
	beam.Attachment1 = a1
	beam.Color = ColorSequence.new((TutorialConfig :: any).BEAM_COLOR or Color3.fromRGB(255, 240, 120))
	local w = (TutorialConfig :: any).BEAM_WIDTH or 1
	beam.Width0 = w
	beam.Width1 = w
	beam.LightEmission = 1
	beam.FaceCamera = true
	beam.Transparency = NumberSequence.new(0.1)
	beam.Parent = root
	state.beam, state.att0, state.att1, state.beamTarget = beam, a0, a1, target
end

local function publish(player: Player, state)
	player:SetAttribute("TutorialStep", state.step)
	player:SetAttribute("TutorialText", textFor(state.step))
	state.nonce += 1
	player:SetAttribute("TutorialNonce", state.nonce)
end

local function cashOf(player: Player): number
	local ls = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
	local c = ls and ls:FindFirstChild("Cash")
	if c and (c:IsA("IntValue") or c:IsA("NumberValue")) then
		return (c :: any).Value
	end
	return 0
end

local function advance(player: Player, state)
	if state.step >= MAX_STEP then
		return
	end
	state.step += 1
	state.startTime = os.clock()
	state.lastReshow = state.startTime
	state.baseCash = cashOf(player)
	publish(player, state)
	ForgeTelemetry.count("tutorial_steps", 1)
	if state.step >= MAX_STEP then
		ForgeTelemetry.count("tutorial_done", 1)
		local tv = player:FindFirstChild("TutorialTarget")
		if tv and tv:IsA("ObjectValue") then
			tv.Value = nil
		end
		clearBeam(state)
	end
end

function TutorialFlow.getStep(player: Player): number
	local s = states[player]
	return if s then s.step else 0
end

function TutorialFlow.notify(player: Player, eventName: string, arg: any?)
	local state = states[player]
	if not state or type(eventName) ~= "string" then
		return
	end
	local step = state.step
	if eventName == "claimed" then
		if step == 1 then
			advance(player, state)
		end
	elseif eventName == "cashed_in" then
		if step == 2 then
			advance(player, state)
		end
	elseif eventName == "upgrade_bought" then
		local id = arg
		if type(id) == "table" then
			id = (id :: any).id or (id :: any).Id
		end
		resolveFirstId()
		if step == 3 then
			if isDropper2(id) or firstUpgradeId == nil then
				advance(player, state)
			end
		elseif step == 5 then
			if id ~= nil and not isDropper2(id) then
				advance(player, state)
			end
		end
	elseif eventName == "shop_opened" then
		if step == 4 then
			ForgeTelemetry.count("shop_opened", 1)
			advance(player, state)
		end
	end
end

local function setupPlayer(player: Player)
	if states[player] then
		return
	end
	local state = {
		step = 1,
		startTime = os.clock(),
		lastReshow = os.clock(),
		nonce = 0,
		baseCash = 0,
	}
	states[player] = state
	local tv = player:FindFirstChild("TutorialTarget")
	if not tv then
		tv = Instance.new("ObjectValue")
		tv.Name = "TutorialTarget"
		tv.Parent = player
	end
	publish(player, state)
end

local function tick(player: Player, state)
	local step = state.step
	if step >= MAX_STEP then
		return
	end
	local now = os.clock()
	if step == 1 and findOwnedPlot(player) then
		advance(player, state)
	elseif step == 2 and cashOf(player) > state.baseCash then
		advance(player, state)
	elseif step == 4 and now - state.startTime >= SHOP_FALLBACK then
		advance(player, state)
	end
	step = state.step
	if step >= MAX_STEP then
		return
	end
	if now - math.max(state.startTime, state.lastReshow) >= STUCK_SECONDS then
		state.lastReshow = now
		publish(player, state)
		ForgeTelemetry.count("tutorial_reshown", 1)
	end
	local target = computeTarget(player, step)
	local tv = player:FindFirstChild("TutorialTarget")
	if tv and tv:IsA("ObjectValue") and tv.Value ~= target then
		tv.Value = target
	end
	updateBeam(player, state, target)
end

function TutorialFlow.start()
	if started then
		return
	end
	started = true

	local remote = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("ShopOpened")
	if not remote or not remote:IsA("RemoteEvent") then
		remote = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
		remote.Name = "ShopOpened"
		remote.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
	end
	(remote :: RemoteEvent).OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player: Player)
		if states[player] and states[player].step == 4 then
			TutorialFlow.notify(player, "shop_opened")
		end
	end)

	Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(setupPlayer)
	for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do
		setupPlayer(p)
	end
	Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
		local s = states[player]
		if s then
			clearBeam(s)
		end
		states[player] = nil
	end)

	task.spawn(function()
		while started do
			task.wait(1)
			for player, state in states do
				if player.Parent then
					local ok = pcall(tick, player, state)
					if not ok then
						continue
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end)
end

return TutorialFlow
```
